changeSet.sql: CREATE TABLE plugin_devicereset_password ( id serial NOT NULL CONSTRAINT plugin_devicereset_password_pr_key PRIMARY KEY, customerId INT NOT NULL REFERENCES customers (id) ON DELETE CASCADE, deviceId INT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices (id) ON DELETE CASCADE, newPassword VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL, requestedBy VARCHAR(100), requestTime BIGINT NOT NULL, deliverTime BIGINT, confirmTime BIGINT, status INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 ); CREATE INDEX plugin_devicereset_password_device_idx ON plugin_devicereset_password (deviceId, status);

changeSet.author: maxcit
changeSet.sql: CREATE TABLE plugin_devicereset_command ( id serial NOT NULL CONSTRAINT plugin_devicereset_command_pr_key PRIMARY KEY, customerId INT NOT NULL REFERENCES customers (id) ON DELETE CASCADE, deviceId INT NOT NULL REFERENCES devices (id) ON DELETE CASCADE, commandType VARCHAR(20) NOT NULL, requestedBy VARCHAR(100), requestTime BIGINT NOT NULL, deliverTime BIGINT, confirmTime BIGINT, status INT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 ); CREATE INDEX plugin_devicereset_command_device_idx ON plugin_devicereset_command (deviceId, status);

changeSet.author: maxcit
changeSet.comment: Rename to Device Management - the plugin now covers several device commands
changeSet.sql: UPDATE plugins SET name = 'Device Management', description = 'Reset the lock screen PIN, reboot and otherwise command a managed device' WHERE identifier = 'devicereset';

changeSet.author: maxcit
changeSet.comment: Table,new: plugin_devicereset_lock - lock is device state, not a one-shot command
changeSet.sql: CREATE TABLE plugin_devicereset_lock ( deviceId INT NOT NULL CONSTRAINT plugin_devicereset_lock_pr_key PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES devices (id) ON DELETE CASCADE, customerId INT NOT NULL REFERENCES customers (id) ON DELETE CASCADE, locked BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE, lockMessage TEXT, requestedBy VARCHAR(100), updateTime BIGINT NOT NULL );

changeSet.author: maxcit
changeSet.comment: Permission,new: plugin_devicereset_wipe - factory reset is irreversible, so it is gated separately from routine PIN resets and reboots

changeSet.author: maxcit
changeSet.comment: Grant plugin_devicereset_wipe to Admin (role 2) as well. In the private usage scenario the account admin is role 2, not Super-Admin, so role 1 alone left nobody able to wipe a device.
changeSet.sql: INSERT INTO userRolePermissions (roleId, permissionId) SELECT 2, p.id FROM permissions p WHERE p.name = 'plugin_devicereset_wipe' AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM userRolePermissions urp WHERE urp.roleId = 2 AND urp.permissionId = p.id);

changeSet.author: maxcit
changeSet.comment: Column,new: deviceCapable - the launcher reports whether it actually has the rights to carry out a command. Without this an admin sees "queued" for a wipe the device already said it cannot perform.
changeSet.sql: ALTER TABLE plugin_devicereset_command ADD COLUMN deviceCapable BOOLEAN;
